disease_label_per_paper: Q fever presenting as recurrent culture-negative endocarditis with aortic prosthesis failure
presentation_summary: 62-year-old man with a mechanical aortic prosthesis had recurrent culture-negative endocarditis/prosthesis failure after prior aortic valve replacement.

Four months after recurrent symptoms and negative blood cultures, re-evaluation showed temperature 36.7 C, blood pressure 158/90 mmHg, heart rate 83/min, basal bilateral fine crackles, no murmur, no splenomegaly, and no peripheral embolic signs.
Laboratory data included hemoglobin 12.4 g/dL, WBC 8.3 x10^9/L, platelets 209 x10^9/L, ESR 32 mm/hr, and CRP 28 mg/L.
TEE and angiography showed a well-fixed aortic prosthesis, absence of vegetations, moderate aortic regurgitation, slight mitral regurgitation, and slight tricuspid regurgitation.
Serology established Q fever and the patient received doxycycline plus hydroxychloroquine; he underwent redo aortic valve replacement for prosthesis failure.

quality_warnings: Coxiella serology is confirmatory, not ordinary ranking evidence.

The ordinary evidence keeps chronic focalized presentation: prosthetic valve substrate, culture-negative endocarditis context, inflammatory markers, valve regurgitation/prosthesis failure, absent visible vegetation, and heart-failure/surgery hazards.
